claim: Co-locating teams by challenge, provisioning 3x device capacity on WiFi and power, and running blind scoring before calibration all improve live event quality
quote: Plan for three times expected device capacity on power and WiFi. Stress-test networks, and maintain backup power generators. Test all audio-visual equipment the day prior to event start.

claim: Tool pricing and credit limits in 2026: Copilot Pro $10/mo with 1,500 credits, Claude Code $17-20/mo, Cursor $20/mo; GitHub Copilot switched to usage-based credits on June 1, 2026
quote: GitHub Copilot: $10/mo (lowest cost, functional free tier) ... Premium request limits (300-1,500/mo) become constraints for heavy agentic use.

claim: Per-tool setup requirements and limitations for Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf/Devin Desktop, and Kiro in June 2026
quote: Windsurf (Now Devin Desktop): Rebranded to Devin Desktop June 2, 2026 (cognition consolidated products under Devin brand). Existing Windsurf accounts carry over.

claim: Live coding display best practices: large font, black on white, clear notifications, maximize windows, reposition tables for sightlines
quote: Use a big font, and maximise the window to ensure visibility from all seats ... Use a black font on a white background rather than light-on-dark schemes for better readability.

claim: Slido, Mentimeter, and ClassPoint pricing and feature comparison for 50-100 person technical workshops; Slido edges out for Q&A upvoting
quote: Slido offers superior Q&A management for technical presentations. ClassPoint provides seamless PowerPoint integration. For 100 developers: ClassPoint Pro (~$8/month) and Slido's Engage tier (~$17.50/month) both comfortably support 100 developers.

claim: VSLive AI Hackathon 2026 used teams of up to 4; judging criteria included architecture, security/safety, business relevance, UX, and use of AI technologies; sending 2-3 devs together yields better outcomes
quote: Solo entries are welcome, and you can form a team of up to 4 members ... The single best decision a dev lead can make is to send people in pairs or small groups.

claim: Hackathon WiFi baseline: 5 Mbps per person; heavy AI development should be segmented onto its own separate Wi-Fi network
quote: We recommend about 5Mbps bandwidth per person ... if you want a specific part of the event to have additional bandwidth, such as AI development or your vendors, this can also be done by putting them each on their own separate Wi-Fi network.

claim: Event WiFi 2026: plan for 1.5+ devices per attendee, no more than 30-50 users per radio, use VLANs to segment traffic, deploy Wi-Fi 6/6E for dense concurrent connections
quote: Plan for 1.5+ devices per attendee ... aim for 30-50 users per radio in high-density areas ... deploy multiple network segments (staff Wi-Fi, attendee Wi-Fi, vendor networks).

claim: Scoring infrastructure: judging module with custom criteria, blind scoring, judge calibration, and transparent shared results improve fairness; set criteria before registration opens
quote: A good judging module lets you set your own criteria, gives judges a simple and clear interface, and produces transparent scores you can share with every team. Implement blind scoring initially to eliminate institutional bias, then conduct judge calibration using sample projects.

claim: Practical AI coding tool evaluation dimensions: technical performance (30%), usability (25%), value (25%), accessibility (20%)
quote: Technical Performance (30%): WebDev AI Leaderboard scores, context window sizes, feature completeness. Practical Usability (25%): Modern web development features, quality and optimization tooling.

claim: VSLive 2026 hackathon ran over two evenings (4-hour blocks), in-person only, with prizes up to $25,000 and five project categories
quote: Tuesday, July 28: 6:00 PM-10:00 PM and Wednesday, July 29: 5:00 PM-9:00 PM, with an Awards Ceremony on Thursday, July 30 from 11:00-11:30am.

claim: Diverse teams with distinct skill sets perform better; pre-event matching by skill profile beats on-the-day random assignment
quote: When looking for teammates, seek out people who are different from you, with unique strengths and abilities from diversity.

claim: Hackathon organization: distribute starter kits and API docs at least one week before the event; use milestone emails to reduce no-shows
quote: Distribute starter kits, API docs, and mentorship schedules at least one week out. Use milestone emails, team formation channels, and pre-event workshops to reduce no-shows.

claim: HackerEarth integrates coding assessments directly into competition workflows; Devpost excels at enterprise-scale reliability for event submissions
quote: Devpost excels at enterprise-scale reliability, while HackerEarth integrates coding assessments directly into competition workflows.

claim: VLANs give each team or segment its own private network, preventing one team's bandwidth-heavy AI agent loop from starving others
quote: VLANs (Virtual Local Area Networks) are individual, secure, private networks so each user has its own network with literally no interference by another developer's bandwidth usage.
